skill.name: god-plan
skill.description: Write a repository-specific plan for a feature or product, with observable requirement checks and ordered implementation steps. Record durable decisions and update project state.
skill.summary: Turn a feature request into a written plan with verifiable requirements and a clear first step.
skill.author: hannsxpeter

security_audit.summary: Nine alerts are Markdown formatting, not Ruby or shell execution. One line directs the agent to run an npm package with automatic confirmation and only a major version specified. No evidence of malicious behavior was found in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.issue: The lint step can execute a newly resolved npm package without a separate confirmation prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a reviewed, repository-local linter installed from a lockfile with integrity checks. Require explicit user approval before fetching or executing any external package.

content.value_statement: Vague feature requests make it hard to agree on what counts as done. This skill writes a plan with observable checks and ordered implementation steps.
actual_capabilities: Reads existing planning files and relevant code to ground the plan in real repository paths.
Writes .godpowers/PLAN.md with scope and detail matched to the request.
Pairs each requirement with a check that a person or a test can perform.
Orders small implementation steps and separates refactors from behavior changes.
Appends lasting decisions and records known risks and the first step in project state.
Asks the user about unresolved questions that block the first step.
limitations: The skill plans work; it does not implement the feature or perform the acceptance checks.
Repository-specific design details depend on access to the relevant files.
The default workflow writes planning files and updates project state. It is not read-only.
The default lint step may fetch and execute an npm package. Review it and authorize it separately.

use_cases.title: Plan a Small Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a defined feature request into a short plan with observable completion checks and a first implementation step.

use_cases.title: Define Product Scope
use_cases.description: Describe success, list what is out of scope, and assign owners to questions that could change the plan.

use_cases.title: Sequence a Technical Change
use_cases.description: Plan a change around existing files and interfaces. Separate behavior changes from refactors and record lasting trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan One Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: A single change with clear scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use god-plan to plan a clear confirmation message after users save their profile. Include the goal, completion checks, and a first step. Do not run the external linter.

prompt_templates.title: Turn Requirements Into Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: A feature brief with requirements already agreed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use god-plan to plan a search filter that applies immediately and clears with one action. Give each requirement an observable check. Do not run the external linter.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Across Existing Components
prompt_templates.scenario: A change that touches several parts of a repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use god-plan to plan saved search presets. Name the existing files involved, cover failure handling, and separate refactors from behavior changes. Ask before running the external linter.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a New Product
prompt_templates.scenario: An early proposal with open design decisions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use god-plan to plan an internal equipment booking tool. Include non-goals, design, decision owners, and a verifiable first step. Record lasting decisions and risks. Ask before running the external linter.

output_examples.input: Plan a confirmation message after a profile save.
output: Goal: Profile editors can tell when a save succeeds.
Done when: A successful save shows a confirmation. A failed save does not show it.
First step: Add the confirmation to the existing save flow and check both outcomes.

output_examples.input: Plan an internal equipment booking tool.
output: Goal: Staff can reserve shared equipment for a time slot.
Non-goal: Access for people outside the organization.
Done when: A second reservation for the same item and time is rejected.
First step: Plan reservation creation and conflict checking as one verifiable change.
Open question: The operations lead decides who can cancel another person's reservation.

best_practices: State who the change serves and what outcome would count as success.
Give each requirement a check that another person can repeat.
Review the plan and state changes before building, and approve external linting separately.
anti_patterns: Use vague checks such as making the feature easier to use without naming an observable result.
Combine unrelated refactors and behavior changes in one implementation step.
Assume a written plan means implementation or verification has already happened.

faq.question: Where does the plan go?
faq.answer: The skill writes the plan to .godpowers/PLAN.md.

faq.question: Does a small request need a full plan?
faq.answer: No. When the requirements are already listed, the plan can focus on the goal, requirements with checks, and ordered implementation steps.

faq.question: What else can the skill update?
faq.answer: It appends lasting choices to DECISIONS.md. It records risks and the first step in STATE.md and sets the stage to build.

faq.question: When does the skill ask for clarification?
faq.answer: It records questions that change the plan and asks you about those that block the first step.

faq.question: Does the skill implement the plan?
faq.answer: No. It describes the work and how to verify it, but does not build the feature.

faq.question: Does the workflow run an external command?
faq.answer: The default workflow requests an npm linter that may fetch and execute package code. Ask to skip it or require approval before it runs.
